title: 第二章 北境少年
content_zh:
骂他的那女人，是大伯母王氏。

    这是原主记忆里告诉江砚的。可他光躺着回想没用，那女人的破锣嗓子已经骂到门口了，门板“哐”地被一脚踹开，半边天的冷风灌进来，王氏叉着腰立在门口，一张黄脸冻得发红，眼睛瞪得溜圆。

    “喊你半天装死呢？”她一把扯住江砚的胳膊，往外拽，“起来起来！白吃白住还想睡到晌午，你当这是你家？”

    江砚被她拽得一个趔趄，几乎栽下炕去。他下意识想发火——在现代，谁敢这么跟他说话——可这具身子太虚了，胳膊被攥得生疼，他一使劲，眼前就发黑，腿肚子直打颤。

    他咬住牙，没吭声，由着王氏把他拖到院里。

    院子比屋里还冷。一层薄雪盖着地，墙角堆着柴火和一口豁了边的水缸，缸里的水结了层冰。三间土坯房，中间那间还算齐整，是大伯一家住的；东头那间塌了半边墙，拿茅草胡乱搭着，就是他原主住的“屋”。猪圈在西墙根，两头瘦得能数出肋骨的猪，正哼哼唧唧拱着空食槽。

    “喂猪、劈柴、把缸里的水挑满。”王氏一样一样数过来，每数一样就用下巴点一下，“晌午前干不完，晚上没你的饭。听见没？”

    江砚抬眼看她。

    就这么一眼，王氏不知怎的，竟被他看得心里咯噔一下。

    往常这小子被骂，从来是缩着脖子、低着头，眼睛盯着自己脚尖，活像挨惯了打的狗。可今天，他直愣愣地看过来，那眼神干净、定，还带着点说不出的、居高临下的冷淡——倒像是她这个当家主母，在被一个外人打量。

    “看什么看！”王氏被那眼神激得心头火起，扬手就要扇过去，“反了你了——”

    江砚没躲。

    不是不想躲，是这具身子太弱，他的脑子让躲，腿却没那么快。那巴掌结结实实落在他脸上，啪的一声脆响，半边脸火辣辣地烧起来，嘴里泛起一丝血腥味。

    院子里安静了一瞬。

    王氏自己都愣了。她打这小子打过不知多少回，可今天这一下，打在那张不躲不闪的脸上，竟让她莫名觉得发虚，像一拳砸进了棉花，又像砸在了石头上。

    江砚慢慢偏过头，把嘴角那点血咽了下去。

    他没哭，也没求饶。他只是在心里，极快地、冷静地，算了一笔账。
content_en:
The woman who scolded him was his aunt Wang.

    This is what the original owner told Jiang Yan in his memory. But it was useless for him to just lie down and think about it. The woman's broken voice had already reached the door. The door panel was kicked open with a kick, and the cold wind from half the sky rushed in. Wang stood at the door with her arms akimbo, her yellow face red from the cold, and her eyes widened.

    "Why are you pretending to be dead for a long time?" She grabbed Jiang Yan's arm and pulled him out, "Get up! You live and eat for free and you want to sleep until noon. Do you think this is your home?"

    Jiang Yan staggered when she pulled him and almost fell off the bed. He subconsciously wanted to get angry - in modern times, who would dare to talk to him like this - but this body was too weak, and his arms were painful from being squeezed. When he exerted force, his eyesight turned black and his calves trembled.

    He gritted his teeth and said nothing, letting Wang drag him to the courtyard.

    The yard is colder than inside. A thin layer of snow covered the ground, and there were firewood piled in the corner and a water tank with a cracked edge. The water in the tank was covered with ice. There are three adobe houses, the one in the middle is relatively neat, and it belongs to the uncle's family; the one in the east has half the wall collapsed, and is built with thatch, which is the "house" where his original owner lived. The pigsty is at the base of the west wall, and two pigs so thin that one can even count their ribs are grunting and digging into the empty trough.

    "Feed the pigs, chop firewood, and fill the tank with water." Wang counted them one by one, tapping her chin every time she counted, "If you can't finish it before noon, you won't have food for the evening. Do you hear me?"

    Jiang Yan looked up at her.

    With just such a look, Wang's heart suddenly trembled at the sight of him.

    Usually when this kid was scolded, he would always shrink his neck, lower his head, and stare at his toes, like a dog that is used to being beaten. But today, he looked over blankly, his eyes clean and steady, with an indescribable, condescending coldness - it seemed as if she, the matron of the house, was being looked at by an outsider.

    "What are you looking at!" Wang's heart was aroused by that look, and she raised her hand to slap him, "I've turned against you——"

    Jiang Yan didn't hide.

    It's not that he doesn't want to hide, it's that his body is too weak. His brain allows him to hide, but his legs are not that fast. The slap landed firmly on his face, with a crisp crack, half of his face burned, and a trace of blood smelled in his mouth.

    The yard was quiet for a moment.

    Wang herself was stunned. She had hit this kid countless times, but today, the blow on that face that refused to dodge made her feel inexplicably weak, like a punch hitting cotton or hitting a stone.

    Jiang Yan slowly turned his head and swallowed the blood at the corner of his mouth.

    He didn't cry or beg for mercy. He just made a calculation in his mind very quickly and calmly.
